evals.prompt: Use the sprint-review-retro skill. Sprint 15 for TaskFlow just ended. Generate a full sprint review report: goal status, completion metrics, what was completed and what was not, velocity trend vs last 3 sprints. Format it so I can demo it to stakeholders. Sprint 15 data: goal 'Ship checkout v2'; 34 of 40 points done and 8 of 10 items done; not delivered: PROJ-312 (3 points, in progress) and PROJ-315 (3 points, blocked); the last three completed sprints delivered 28, 31 and 30 points. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it brief: no preamble, the key points and calls first, about 15 lines in all.
evals.expected_output: Stakeholder-ready review: sprint name + dates + goal, completion rate in points and item count, Delivered table (ID/title/points/owner), Not Delivered list with reasons, velocity comparison to previous 3 sprints, goal achievement verdict (Yes/Partial/No).
expectations: The answer says to get the sprint with cycle(action=list, status=completed)
The answer says to count the items per state group with workitem(action=count, pql='cycle = "<cycle_id>"', group_by=state__group)
The answer shows the line Completion: 34/40 points (85%)
The answer shows the line Items: 8/10 completed
The answer says to transfer PROJ-312 (in progress) to the next sprint
The answer says to list PROJ-312 and PROJ-315 under NOT COMPLETED

evals.prompt: Use the sprint-review-retro skill. Run a retrospective for Sprint 14. Use the DAKI format. Previous retro's action items were: (1) 'Review PRs within 4 hours' - done, (2) 'Set up staging deploy' - still open. Give the order of the session, the new action items you propose, and what gets recorded in Plane and how. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it brief: no preamble, the key points and calls first, about 15 lines in all.
evals.expected_output: Starts with previous action review, shows DAKI prompts, creates 2-3 new action items with SMART criteria, saves as a page.
expectations: The answer reviews the two previous action items before it opens the DAKI prompts
The answer says to use the four DAKI headings DROP, ADD, KEEP and IMPROVE
The answer limits the new action items to 2-3
The answer says to create each action item with workitem(action=create) and a name that starts with [RETRO]
The answer says to label the action items with retro-action
The answer says to save the notes with page(action=create) under a name like Retro — Sprint 14 (YYYY-MM-DD)

evals.prompt: Use the sprint-review-retro skill. Sprint 14 is done. 3 items still in progress, 1 blocked, 1 not started. Walk me through closing the sprint. Show each call in order with its parameters, and say what happens to each of the five unfinished items. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it brief: no preamble, the key points and calls first, about 15 lines in all.
evals.expected_output: Take blocked and not-started items out of the cycle (cycle manage_workitems remove_ids) so they return to the backlog, complete the cycle, transfer the remaining unfinished in-progress items to the next cycle, then archive the current cycle.
expectations: The answer says to remove the blocked and the not-started item with cycle(action=manage_workitems, remove_ids=[...]) before the transfer
The answer says to create the next cycle with cycle(action=create, ..., owned_by=...)
The answer says to end the sprint with cycle(action=complete) before the transfer
The answer says to move the three in-progress items with cycle(action=transfer_workitems, cycle_id, new_cycle_id)
The answer says to archive the sprint with cycle(action=archive) as the last call
The answer says to record completed_points for the velocity history

evals.prompt: Use the sprint-review-retro skill. Our last 4 sprints completed at 65%, 68%, 72%, 60%. Retro action items rarely get done. What should the retro facilitator focus on? Say what the numbers mean, what to change about the next commitment, and how the retro should handle action items. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses completion rate as WARNING (<70% consistently), action items as WARNING. Suggests reducing commitment by 20% and limiting retro to ONE action item to improve follow-through.
expectations: The answer says to read completion rates against the health metrics thresholds
The answer flags commitment as too aggressive (reduce by 20%)
The answer flags low action item follow-through as a process issue
The answer recommends limiting to 1 action item until follow-through improves
The answer suggests reviewing previous actions at the START of each retro for accountability
